overview: The LAAA Team of Marcus & Millichap is pleased to present 2540 S Barrington Avenue, a 12-unit apartment building in West Los Angeles. The two-story wood frame building was completed in 1958 and holds ten one bedroom and two two bedroom units, 6,535 square feet on an 8,257 square foot R4-1 lot. The units open onto a courtyard pool. The building is registered under the Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance.

The investment case is rent growth on turnover in a building with one ownership since 1978. Scheduled rent of $251,328 grows to $292,800 at market, about 16.5% upside. Four tenancies that began between 1999 and 2018 pay $1,170 to $1,352, and the two units open on the August 2026 rent roll can be leased at market now.

The block is 0.7 miles from the Expo/Sepulveda E Line station, and the R4-1 lot allows about 20 units under base zoning against 12 today, a long-term option for a patient owner. The offering fits 1031 exchange buyers and West Los Angeles apartment owners who hold for the long term.
location_narrative: The property sits on Barrington Avenue just south of Gateway Boulevard in the Sawtelle pocket of West Los Angeles, about 0.3 miles south of Pico Boulevard. Whole Foods Market on National Boulevard is 0.47 miles southeast and Marukai Market on Pico 0.49 miles west. Walk Score rates the block 76, carried by the restaurants at the Barrington and Gateway corner.

The Expo/Sepulveda station on the Metro E Line is 0.7 miles northeast, putting Santa Monica and Downtown Los Angeles on one rail line. The I-10 is about 570 feet south. Sony Pictures Studios is 2.49 miles east, Westfield Century City 2.51 miles northeast, UCLA 2.82 miles north and Santa Monica Place 3.09 miles west.

ZIP 90064 is 51% renter occupied, with a median household income of $135,383 and a median gross rent of $2,855 (2024 American Community Survey). Of its 12,954 housing units, 6,064 were built before 1960. The Exposition Corridor Transit Neighborhood Plan rezoned about 256 acres along the E Line for about 6,000 additional homes by 2035.
physical_narrative: The building is a two-story Type V wood frame apartment house completed in 1958, 6,535 square feet on an 8,257 square foot lot, laid out in a U around the courtyard pool with a laundry room. It holds ten one bedroom one bath units of about 500 square feet and two two bedroom units of about 700 square feet; unit sizes are estimates from the county's gross area.
All 45 windows were replaced with dual glazing in 2012, and a pool bonding permit was finaled the same year. Parking is at the rear of the building; the stall count is being confirmed with the owner.
market_narrative: Fifteen City of Los Angeles apartment sales of 8 to 14 units, built 1953 to 1973, closed between September 2024 and August 2026 at a median of $258,333 per unit, $341 per SF and 11.30 times rent. The closest match, 11296 Brookhaven Avenue, 12 units built in 1958 half a mile away, sold for $3.1M in September 2025 at 11.56 times rent, with the seller's low-rate loan taken over by the buyer. 1519 Armacost Avenue, 11 small units, closed in July 2026 at 10.48 times rent and a 5.89% cap.

Thirty days before each of those sales closed, the 5-year Treasury ran 3.61% to 4.40%, a median of 3.91%. On 09/22/2026 it stood at 4.83% (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED series DGS5). The four closings from June to August 2026, which locked nearest today's rates, ran 9.16 to 11.19 times rent.
A buyer today pays about a point more for money than the buyers who set most of those comps, so the 2026 closings carry more weight in our pricing than the 2024 and 2025 sales.
positioning_narrative: The right buyer wants a Westside pool building near two rail stations, four legacy tenancies to turn over time and an R4 lot to hold. We would qualify buyers early on their financing, because at today's rates the loan decides what a buyer can pay.
rent_narrative: Unrenovated one bedrooms in 1950s and 1960s buildings within 1.5 miles came off the market at $1,995 to $2,240 this year, in units of 625 to 650 SF where the listing gives a size, and a renovated 610 SF unit at 2650 S Barrington Avenue came off the market at $2,300. Two bedroom one baths ran $2,495 to $2,995 in 775 to 900 SF units, including 11562 Gateway Boulevard, which came off the market at $2,700 after ten days.

Market rent is $1,950 for a one bedroom of about 500 SF, in line with the building's own one bedroom leases since 2023, and $2,450 for a two bedroom of about 700 SF. Unit 6 has not leased at its $2,600 ask, so the two bedroom market rent is set below it. The pro forma carries every unit at those rents.
valuation_narrative: The recommended list price is $2.6M, $216,667 per unit and $398 per SF, with an opinion of value of $2.55M to $2.65M. Current scheduled rent of $251,328, with units 3 and 6 at market, less a 3% vacancy reserve and plus $1,070 of laundry income gives $244,858 of effective gross income. Operating expenses of $104,769, with taxes reassessed at the list price, leave net operating income of $140,089: a 5.39% cap rate and a 10.35 gross rent multiplier. At market rents the net operating income is $178,708, a 6.87% cap rate.

The price sits at 10.35 times rent, below the 10.48 to 11.56 range of the closest sales, and at $216,667 per unit, in the lower third of the set. The 5.39% cap reflects a full expense load for a pool building, including insurance at $1,300 per unit and reserves at $400 per unit. Those comps priced on cheaper money; at this price a buyer who finances half at today's 6.75% still covers debt service 1.38 times.

claims.text: 12535 Pacific is priced above that escrow figure, at $238,889 per unit and 10.76 times rent, because the buildings differ. Its soft-story retrofit was completed in 2018. Five of its nine units have been re-leased near market, including two bedroom two baths at $2,700 in November 2024 and $2,750 in September 2026, above the $2,595 two bedroom market rent in 12231's own model, where the in-place two bedrooms rent for $1,643 to $2,120. It has no open city orders, while the housing department's 2026 orders on 12231's exterior balconies and walkways remain open on the public record. It also has nine units to 12231's seven, four of them legacy tenancies with room to grow on turnover.

Scheduled rent is the owner's August 2026 rent roll, with unit 7 at its new lease from 09/06/2026 and unit 2 at market rent. Taxes are reassessed at 1.1874% of the list price plus $1,322 of direct assessments. Insurance is an estimate of $1,100 per unit; utilities, trash and service contracts follow the owner's 2026 statements; repairs ($800 per unit), reserves ($250 per unit) and management (4% of effective gross income) are LAAA allowances. No on-site manager expense is carried. Financing shown is an illustrative new loan at 50% of price, 6.75% and 30-year amortization at today's rates.

Comparable sale prices come from TheMLS and county records. Cap rates on the comparable sales are LAAA estimates built from each building's own MLS income with a 3% vacancy and taxes restated at the sale price. 12231 Pacific Avenue figures come from the LAAA Team's own listing file and are final when the sale closes. Rent comparables are asking rents and listings removed from the market, which suggests a lease without proving one. Unit square footages are estimates.
